title: Surge-aware alert provisioning with compact shift baton and postmortem deep-links
creator: Marin Ortega
description: Problem statement: On-call responders frequently face alert surges that make existing alertsetup flows and handoff surfaces noisy and slow. We need a compact provisioning flow that is surge-aware (shows suggested dedupe/threshold policies during high-volume windows), a lightweight 'shift baton' UI for quick transfer of ownership, and persistent postmortem deep-links so investigators can jump from an alert to the right retrospectives and metrics.
mvp: 1) Alert provisioning wizard that surface surge-aware suggestions and a quick 'apply' path. 2) Compact Shift Baton card on alert detail for one-click transfer with context. 3) Postmortem deep-link slot on alert timeline that auto-populates runbook and postmortem draft link.
success_metrics: Reduce mean time to assign alert owner by 30% during peak windows
Increase use of recommended alert thresholds by 40%
deliverables: Figma prototype: surge-aware wizard flow (desktop + narrow)
High-fidelity Shift Baton component (compact and expanded) with microcopy
Interaction spec for postmortem deep link generation and UX state transitions
Design QA checklist and accessibility notes
acceptance_criteria: Surge-aware suggestions show for >80% of simulated high-volume scenarios in lab test
Shift Baton transfers ownership without requiring page reload and shows confirmation toast
Postmortem deep-link appears in timeline for alerts with linked incidents and opens draft PM doc template
design_notes: We intentionally collapse threshold controls into a single slider + presets to avoid overwhelming users during surges.
Presets: conservative / balanced / aggressive. Each preset displays expected alert rate delta and downstream incident probability (experimental).
Shift Baton shows: current owner avatar, on-call schedule peek, suggested recipients based on recent activity and escalation policies.
Postmortem deep-link uses incident tags + timeline anchors so link opens at the earliest correlated event in the postmortem draft.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: prefer minimal inline edits during surge to avoid accidental config churn; advanced full editor tucked behind 'Edit advanced' link.
Tradeoff: showing predicted incident probability requires a simple ML heuristic from ENG-2309; we will ship a conservative deterministic fallback if scoring service is unavailable.
Decision: Shift Baton will not auto-reassign on timeout for MVP; it will only propose reassignment and require explicit confirm to keep behavior predictable.

dev_feedback: Preference for optimistic UI on baton transfer and ephemeral local undo (5s) — reduces perceived latency
Batch preset application should be idempotent; backend to return a change diff for UI confirmation
accessibility_considerations: Ensure Shift Baton control is keyboard focusable and has clear ARIA labels for ownership change
Provide text-only fallback for surge suggestions; color not sole indicator
user_research: Interview summary: 6 responders; common pain points — noisy threshold config, fear of changing rules in surge, difficulty finding postmortems after incident closure
Key quote: 'When things spike I just want the system to give me a safe, reversible nudge'
prototype_notes: Prototype includes two surge scenarios: 'bursty alerts from a single service' and 'cross-service noise during deploys'
Narrow viewport tested: baton density reduced to icon+initials with expand affordance
Microcopy draft for confirmation: 'Transfer ownership to {{name}}? This will notify them and annotate the incident.'
qa_and_testing_plan: Simulated surge harness with synthetic alerts (coord with ENG-3120)
End-to-end test for baton transfer via Cypress (happy path + undo)
Permission matrix test to validate postmortem link visibility across roles
